en: Curation is deciding what will be seen, rewarded and repeated, like someone putting together an exhibition. Here it is so intense, so hyper, that it comes to govern time and to sell the waiting itself. It looks like nothing more than nice advertising, but it works as a method that turns expectation into a regular way of keeping things valuable. And it makes a promise about the future without giving you, in the same measure, a way to check whether that promise will be kept.

Many skins go beyond an image pasted onto the character, and some change shape during the match itself, with transformations, effects and animations. This only happens if the game remains able to draw models, effects, animations and screens, which are remade with every update.

In an online game, the account holds characters, skins, emotes and the game's currency, and none of it leaves the account. Behind the login and password sit the inventory, the progress, the player name and the signals by which others recognize you.

That is why you can read every line of the terms of use and still be unable to check whether you received what was promised. Not for lack of attention, but because the meaning of things in there is set by rules and records you do not control. More than knowing little, the problem is being unable to verify, understand and contest in an environment someone else organizes.
